title: NimbleCart QBR - Degradation, SLA & Cost Playbook Sync
summary: Quarterly health review focused on recent degradation incidents, clarifying SLA expectations, and establishing a cost-latency playbook for upcoming holiday traffic. Agreed to run a targeted latency baseline and a dedicated pilot with prefix caching and adjusted batching/quantization profiles.
topics: security & compliance asks: SOC 2, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-22 15:00 UTC | Duration ~60m | Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Maya (CSM), Priya (NimbleCart Head ML), Marco (Platform), Ellen (FinOps), Tom (SRE)

[00:00:03] Sofia: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll try to keep this tight, we had a short agenda, the degradation post-mortem, then sla clarifications and cost playbook for holiday ramp.
[00:00:18] Priya: thanks, yeah appreciate it. quick context, last week we saw tail latency spikes during peak checkout flows, about 600 requests over a 10-minute window, p95 moved from 120ms to 560ms, some requests timed out.
[00:00:34] Tom: right, from our side the error budget alarm tripped, paging went off, SIEM flagged some retries.
[00:00:42] Liam: okay, thanks for that. we dug into the traces and saw sustained KV cache misses + overloaded batching lanes. looks like the requests hit the larger sequence path and pushed the runtime into a different kernel selection, plus a suboptimal autoscale window.
[00:01:00] Marco: i'm not 100% sure i follow — "KV cash" misses? do you mean the key-value cache for decoder?
[00:01:08] Liam: yeah sorry, kv cache, sometimes transcribed as K-V cash in the logs. so prefix cache wasn't used for those sessions because of a header mismatch from the gateway. small config thing but big perf delta.
[00:01:22] Ellen: is that something we can patch quickly or is infra change?
[00:01:26] Liam: quick fix — gateway header normalization — should be a config rollout. medium term we'd recommend pinning a dedicated pool for checkout-critical routes to avoid noisy-neighbor batching.
[00:01:38] Sofia: to add, there's tradeoffs: dedicated reduces tail latency variance but costs more. for holiday you probably want a hybrid: dedicated small pool + hosted fallback.
[00:01:50] Priya: our main questions are SLA guarantees and if Redwood can commit to p99 under load, and what observability we get into token-level latency and cost.
[00:01:59] Maya: we can give token-level traces in the console, and the dedicated plan includes more detailed traces and longer retention for debug windows.
[00:02:10] Tom: what about cold starts? we saw slowdowns when a new pod came up.
[00:02:15] Liam: cold start is usually about model warmup and kv cache; for TGI it takes a few steps to fill the cache. we recommend warmup hooks or a tiny pre-warming pool during traffic ramp.
[00:02:28] Priya: ok timeline — can you run a baseline test before Black Friday? we need a 2x scale verification.
[00:02:33] Sofia: absolutely. next step we'll propose a pilot: dedicated pool + prefix caching + adjusted batching profile and a quantized model variant for cheaper tokens.
[00:02:45] Marco: quantized variant — do you expect quality regression? our checkout NLU is sensitive to hallucinations.
[00:02:51] Liam: good call out. quantization helps cost but can alter logits; we'll run head-to-head evals on your prompt set. Redwood Optimize will flag regressions and we can rollback to float if thresholds are crossed.
[00:03:06] Ellen: cost — we need an estimate delta, dedicated vs hosted. our CFO asked for worst-case burn for holiday.
[00:03:13] Sofia: we'll send an econ sheet. rough ballpark: dedicated small pool + burst capacity gives predictable throughput; you trade some unit-cost increase for latency SLOs. the Optimize recommendations can drop unit tokens by ~15-30% with caching+batch tweaks.
[00:03:28] Priya: security: we need SOC 2 evidence, KMS integration, and vendor audit logs. do you support customer-managed keys?
[00:03:35] Maya: yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM with customer-managed keys and full audit logs; hosted customers can opt for encryption at rest with Redwood-managed keys but enterprise plans include KMS integration.
[00:03:46] Tom: also SSO and RBAC — we need per-team role separation and SAML SSO.
[00:03:51] Sofia: SSO/SAML, RBAC, and scim provisioning are on the enterprise console. we'll share the security pack.
[00:03:59] Marco: any gotchas around VPC peering or on-prem?
[00:04:03] Liam: for private deployment we offer a VPC connector set; on-prem is possible but requires a packaged deployment and a longer lead time for firewall rules and KMS setups.
[00:04:14] Ellen: is the audit trail tamper-evident?
[00:04:17] Maya: yes we provide immutable audit logs and export hooks (S3) for your SIEM.
[00:04:23] Priya: back to the incident: what would you have done to avoid it?
[00:04:27] Liam: two things: tighter request header validation so prefix caching isn't disabled by gateway mutations; and an autoscale policy tuned for short spikes plus conservative batching thresholds to avoid large sequence lanes filling small ones.
[00:04:42] Tom: can batching be per-route? we don't want chat paths to affect checkout.
[00:04:45] Sofia: yes, Redwood routes can be per-endpoint and you can set isolated batching windows, model variants, and prioritization.
[00:04:54] Marco: do you have any best practices doc for checkout-critical flows?
[00:04:58] Liam: we'll share a playbook — includes prefix caching, route isolation, warmup hooks, and quantization guidance.
[00:05:05] Ellen: actionable KPIs we want: p95/p99 latency, error budget consumption, cost per checkout.
[00:05:11] Sofia: noted. we'll craft the pilot success criteria around those.
[00:05:16] Priya: what about rolling upgrades and canary? we push model rollouts frequently.
[00:05:20] Liam: Redwood supports canary splits and automatic rollback on quality regression tied to your eval set. we can do traffic-based canaries or request-based canaries by header.
[00:05:31] Priya: great. for the pilot duration how long?
[00:05:34] Sofia: recommend 2 weeks of soak under simulated peak, plus a 48-hour ramp to validate autoscale.
[00:05:41] Marco: simulation — can Redwood run a golden load test or do we run our own scripts?
[00:05:46] Liam: we can run synthetic load tests in partnership, but we'd prefer using your replay data for realism. we'll sign an MSA addendum for data replay if needed.
[00:05:56] Ellen: billing — how will this be invoiced? reserved vs burst, and what happens if we exceed commit?
[00:06:02] Sofia: dedicated reserved capacity is invoice monthly; burst overage can be charged per-token or moved to hosted fallback. we'll send a clear pricing scenario and a worst-case projection.
[00:06:12] Priya: ok, can we walk through a hypothetical incident timeline with on-call? who gets paged?
[00:06:19] Maya: Redwood provides alert hooks, and the dedicated plan adds an escalation path to SEs during business hours; for 24/7 we have an addon.
[00:06:28] Tom: we want a runbook — steps, contacts, and rollback buttons.
[00:06:31] Liam: we'll draft a runbook and include runbook commands in the console (scale down, pin variant, revert model).
[00:06:39] Priya: can you summarize pilot scope?
[00:06:42] Sofia: sure — small dedicated checkout pool, prefix caching enforcement, adjusted batching profile, quantized model variant with eval guardrails, pre-warm during ramp, 2-week soak, synthetic + replayed load test, runbook and monitoring dashboards, security checklist for KMS and SSO.
[00:07:00] Marco: success metrics again?
[00:07:02] Sofia: p99 < 250ms for checkout flows during peak, <2% error budget consumption per day, cost per checkout within agreed threshold (we'll provide three scenarios: conservative, expected, worst-case).
[00:07:14] Ellen: timeline to get pilot started?
[00:07:17] Sofia: we can get a pilot kickoff next week pending legal; security docs and pricing to be shared within 48 hours.
[00:07:24] Priya: good. any blockers for us?
[00:07:26] Maya: need your security contact to sign the KMS addendum and a replay dataset sample.
[00:07:30] Tom: will do.
[00:07:32] Sofia: perfect.
[00:07:34] [~end of core discussion — additional Q&A and wrap] 
[00:07:40] Marco: small nit — does Redwood autobalance across regions if we have users in EU/NA?
[00:07:45] Liam: yes route-based regional placement and fallback; we can pin region per-route with latency routing policies.
[00:07:52] Priya: competitor question — how this differs from running on-prem with our own GPUs?
[00:07:56] Sofia: main diff is operational overhead: Redwood handles kernel selection, continuous batching, and live fallbacks; on-prem gives full control but you own ops and failover. Dedicated with Redwood gives you most of the predictability without full ops burden.
[00:08:10] Ellen: understood. thanks everyone.
[00:08:13] Sofia: last bit — recap and owners.

Recap: run pilot for checkout-critical flows: dedicated pool + caching + batching + quantized evals + pre-warm; security docs and pricing in 48h; kickoff next week pending legal.
